# zlanhe

> Computes the value of the one-norm, Frobenius norm, infinity-norm, or the.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlanhe from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlanhe';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlanhe( order, norm, uplo, N, A, LDA, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Input array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHE as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the hermitian matrix A is to be referenced.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part of A is referenced
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part of A is referenced
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHE is set to zero.
- `A`: The hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading n by n upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading n by n lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that the imaginary parts of the diagonal elements need not be set and are assumed to be zero.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: output array

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlanhe.ndarray(
    norm, uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × N</sub> | Complex Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | First dimension stride for A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride for A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace array (length >= N for `'one-norm'`/`'inf-norm'` norms) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHE as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the hermitian matrix A is to be referenced.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular part of A is referenced
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular part of A is referenced
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHE is set to zero.
- `A`: The hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading n by n upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading n by n lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that the imaginary parts of the diagonal elements need not be set and are assumed to be zero.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlanhe from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlanhe';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = zlanhe( 'row-major', 'one-norm', 'upper', N, A, N, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zlanhe.ndarray( 'one-norm', 'upper', N, A, N, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANHE`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANHE returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a complex hermitian matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANHE} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(`A(i,j)`)) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
